title: Tile-aware precision router with minimal dequant exposure
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight, tile-aware precision routing layer that picks INT8 / FP8 / mixed microkernel implementations per-attention-tile to minimize end-to-end dequantization overhead and preserve decode latency SLAs.

Rationale: Current coarse-grained precision routing forces full-layer dequantization or conservative FP8 execution which increases cost or latency. By scoring tiles (sub-blocks of attention heads x token ranges) we can route only the tiles that benefit from lower precision to INT8 microkernels and avoid widespread dequant where it is unnecessary. This reduces token-level compute and memory pressure while keeping decode jitter low.

Success metrics (targeted):
- 8-15% reduction in median decode latency on streaming workloads that have short tail tokens (<= 50 tokens).
- <= 2% quality regression measured on our eval prompt set (if exceeded, fallback thresholds tighten).
- 10-20% reduction in total token compute cost for mixed workloads (chat + retrieval).

Design summary:
- Tile definition: 8-head x 64-token sub-blocks (configurable). Router computes a lightweight score per tile from three signals: headwise variance (SNR proxy), token density (non-pad fraction), and cached-kv-hit ratio.
- Decision policy: score -> discrete action {INT8_fast, INT8_precise, FP8, FP32-fallback} using a small decision table tuned offline.
- Minimal dequant strategy: dequantization is deferred and localized: INT8 tiles remain in compact quantized buffers through attention compute and only dequant when aggregating outputs for the subset of tiles that must be merged into mixed-precision outputs. Where possible we perform accumulation in quantized-friendly epilogues to avoid full-canvas dequant.
- Kernel integration: implement a routing shim that selects tile-level microkernels (existing INT8 microkernel, FP8 microkernel) and orchestrates zero-copy handoff of KV slices. New microkernel hooks expose required interfaces: partial-accumulate, quant-epilogue, and headwise-scale-adapter.
- KV layout: extend existing KV slab to tag tile ranges with precision metadata and scaling factors. This allows selective decode reuse without inflating memory for FP paths.
- Telemetry & safety: add per-tile telemetry (latency, error proxy) and an online lightweight quality gate that forces FP8 if a tile's scaled error exceeds threshold. System includes backpressure to avoid oscillation.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike (done): tile scoring prototype in runtime-sim with synthetic inputs.
2) Prototype kernel shim + KV tags: wire router to existing INT8/FP8 kernels; validate memory safety.
3) Microbench + eval: end-to-end bench on g4dn-like and A100 setups; run evals for quality.
4) Canary rollout: enable on limited percentage for hosted workloads and monitor cost/quality dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
- Router selects INT8 path for at least 25% of tiles on targeted workloads with measured latency improvement and no more than 2% eval degradation.
- No user-facing regressions in streaming token ordering or token emission latency.
- Feature flippable via runtime flag and covered by unit + e2e tests.

Constraints and open questions:
- Interaction with continuous batching: batching policies may blur tile boundaries; need to ensure router decisions are compatible with batch coalescing.
- Garbage collection of mixed-precision KV slabs under high-concurrency workloads.
- Kernel API changes must remain ABI-compatible for older microkernels until rollout completes.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Spike summary: implemented a prototype tile scorer that uses head-variance and token density; synthetic microbench shows 9% median latency reduction for 32-token streams when routing 30% of tiles to INT8. Notes in Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runtime/tile-router-spike

2026-02-18 - Design sync with ML infra and kernels team. Decision: use 8x64 tile defaults, support tuning via per-customer profile. Action: Diego to draft kernel shim API. (meeting notes: https://drive.internal/redwood/meetings/2026-02-18-tile-router)

2026-02-24 - Prototype integration: added KV slab tags and routed INT8 microkernel for tile-local attention. Observed unexpected copy during int8->fp8 merge path; root cause: accumulator epilogue didn't expose partial-accumulate interface. Filed follow-up ENG-946102 for microkernel epilogue changes.

2026-02-28 - Microbench results: A100 tests show 11% median latency win and 14% p95 improvement on conversational throughput when ~35% of tiles picked INT8. Quality eval on core prompt set: 1.6% BLEU-equivalent metric drop; within threshold. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/runtime/tile-router/overview

2026-03-02 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2761. PR includes router shim, KV-tagging, and microkernel selection hooks. TODO: add unit tests for fallbacks and batching interaction. Assigned reviewers: @maria-gonzales, @kevin-choi

2026-03-05 - Code review feedback: address 1) race on KV tag updates under concurrent writes, 2) add better observability for tile decision rationale, 3) add canary rollout flag and runtime knob for tile-size. Diego updated PR with fixes; awaiting final review.
